THREE items straddle the gutter and were read c1-then-c2 as instructed: 28 (statements + options a,b in c1; options c,d in c2), 32 (statements in c1; the 'Which one of the following' line + all four options in c2), 39 (pair table in c1; the 'How many of the above pairs' line + all four options in c2). All eight column crops were clean - no sliced lines, no missing item number at the top of a c2, no fragment of the neighbouring column. VERBATIM ODDITIES, all transcribed as printed and not normalised: item 37 prints options (b) 'I and III' and (d) 'II and III' WITHOUT the word 'only' that (a) and (c) carry; item 40 prints (a) 'I and II' and (c) 'I and III' without 'only'; item 39 option (d) reads 'All the five'; item 38 prints its decimal as '0·5' with a raised/middle dot (the UPSC house convention) and sets CO2 with a true subscript, transcribed as LaTeX. Item 39's Plant/Description pair list is a genuine two-column grid in the booklet (headers printed in bold, ':' separating the columns) and is rendered as a GFM pipe table with its separator row; the ':' column separators were dropped because the pipes carry that job. Items 27-34 are all 'Statement I/II(/III)' items and 31, 32, 33 and 34 share a character-identical four-option block with 28 - that is the paper's own repeated format, not a transcription slip.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements :
Statement I :
In January, in the Northern Hemisphere, the isotherms bend equatorward while crossing the landmasses, and poleward while crossing the oceans.
Statement II :
In January, the air over the oceans is warmer than that over the landmasses in the Northern Hemisphere.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

options.label: A
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I

options.label: B
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I

options.label: C
options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct

options.label: D
options.text: Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
